text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Government may retain a majority share in joint-venture oil operations, petroleum minister Dan Etete said in India during the International Energy Conference.

- Chief of General Staff General Oladipo Diya explains government's decision to allow private participation in the power industry as an effort to give an efficient and stable power supply to the nation.
- The Nigerian Textile Manufacturers Association has attributed the industry's declining fortunes to smuggling of clothes from China, Taiwan and Indonesia.
- Nigeria's second highest ruling body, the National Council of State, will meet on Tuesday to discuss ways in which the electoral commission can be helped to conduct local government elections.
- Three months after the official deregulation of interest rates it is yet to have any effect on transactions in the capital market.
- Nigeria recorded a trade surplus with Japan of $13.2 million in the first six months of this year, largely as a result of Japan's oil imports.
